newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan October trade surplus down yr/yr 62.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan October trade surplus down yr/yr 62.2 pct.

text.p: Taiwan had a trade surplus of US$532.4 million in October, down 62.2 percent from a surplus of US$1.410 billion in October 1995, the finance ministry said on Thursday.
The following is a table of trade figures in millions of U.S. dollars:
October 1996 October 1995
Imports 9,289 9,095
Trade balance +532 +1,410
Exports in October fell 6.5 percent from October 1995 to US$9.821 billion, while imports rose a year-on-year 2.1 percent to $9.289 billion, the ministry said in a statement.
The cumulative surplus for the first 10 months of 1996 was $10.691 billion, up 98 percent from the same 1995 period, it said.
Exports for the first 10 months totalled $95.426 billion, and imports stood at $84.735 billion, the ministry said.
The ministry attributed October's reduced trade surplus to a decline in exports -- led by an 18.7 percent fall in exports from Taiwan's bedrock electronics sector.
The report played down the downturn, noting that the export total in October 1995 was a historic monthly high and that October 1996 exports were the fourth-highest on record.
The United States was Taiwan's top export destination in October. Exports to the U.S. fell 1.5 percent to $2.394 billion, accounting for 24.4 percent of the monthly total.
Exports to Hong Kong were down 2.8 percent to $2.262 billion and exports to Japan fell 18.5 percent to $1.032 billion.
Exports to Europe fell 4.7 percent to $1.456 billion, comprising 14.8 percent of the total.
Imports from Japan fell 13.6 percent in October to $2.226 billion, or 24 percent of the total.
Imports from the United States dropped five percent to $1.642 billion, or 17.7 percent of the total.
Taiwan's monthly trade surplus with the United States was at $752 million, up 6.9 percent from October 1995.
The surplus with Hong Kong fell 1.9 percent to $2.116 billion from a year ago.
The deficit with Japan was down 8.7 percent to $1.193 billion. Taiwan recorded a deficit with Europe of $543 million, against a deficit of $46.3 million in October 1995.
The ministry said it expected both exports and imports to rise in the near future due to steady growth in the global economy and easing tensions between Taiwan and China.
Electronic equipment and machinery remained the star sector of Taiwan's exports in October, totalling $4.567 billion or 46.5 percent of overall exports.
-- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
